front: What is Decision tree in one sentence?

front: Explain the mental model of Decision tree (how the system thinks).
back: A decision tree asks a sequence of yes/no questions on one feature at a time until a leaf assigns a class (classification) or average target (regression).

Production latency at massive depth — shallow tree or linear model; …

front: What is Mean Average Precision (MAP) in one sentence?
back: Ranking metric: average of per-query Average Precision — rewards relevant items ranked high — IR evaluation (Manning, Raghavan, Schütze).

front: Explain the mental model of Mean Average Precision (MAP) (how the system thinks).
back: For each query, you have a ranked list of items. Relevance is binary (or graded in nDCG). Precision@k = relevant in top k / k. Average Precision (AP) integrates precision at each rank where a relevant item appears.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Mean Average Precision (MAP)?
back: MAP cares about order: putting all relevant items at the top scores higher than burying one relevant doc at rank 50.

front: Given a broken Mean Average Precision (MAP) setup, what is your first validation command?
back: MAP cares about order: putting all relevant items at the top scores higher than burying one relevant doc at rank 50.

front: What are the production-safe defaults for Mean Average Precision (MAP)?
back: 1. Hold out queries with labeled relevant set (clicks, purchases, human grades). 2. Score all candidates; sort descending. 3. Report MAP @ full list and Precision@5 / Recall@20 for product SLAs.

front: Symptom: MAP = 1.0 suspiciously — what do you check and fix?

front: Symptom: MAP flat despite "better" model — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Wrong labels (implicit vs explicit) · Fix: Define relevance from business event

front: Symptom: Offline MAP ↑, revenue flat — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Position bias in logs · Fix: Inverse propensity scoring; interleaving

front: Symptom: AP undefined — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: No relevant items in query · Fix: Skip query or define fallback metric

front: Symptom: Compares unfairly across systems — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Different candidate pools · Fix: Same corpus per query

front: Gotcha with Mean Average Precision (MAP): what silently fails?
back: MAP with binary relevance ignores how relevant (marginally vs perfect match) — use Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG) for graded labels.

front: When should you NOT use Mean Average Precision (MAP)?
back: Single-label classification — use precision/recall/F1 (binary classification). Regression — use MAE/RMSE (regression). Clustering — no query-level ranking.

front: What is Binary Classification?
back: Effective for linearly separable data (can separate two classes with a straight line).

front: What is Linear Limitation?
back: Can only classify linearly separable data. It struggles with complex data that can't be separated by a straight line (e.g., XOR problem).

front: What is Single Layer?
back: The basic perceptron is limited to binary classification and can't handle multi-class problems or complex patterns. This is why multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) and more complex neural networks are often used.

front: What is Random forest in one sentence?

front: Explain the mental model of Random forest (how the system thinks).
back: Why it works: individual trees overfit; averaging uncorrelated errors reduces variance without heavy bias increase. Random feature subsampling at splits decorrelates trees beyond bagging alone.

Linear separable with sparse high-dim text — linear models + hashing faster and simpler. Strict latency (< few ms) on edge — model size of hundreds of trees may exceed budget; linear or tiny NN. Online learning — full retrain required; not incremental.
